Rashi on Ketubot 70b:10:1.hebrew: ופרנס לאו שליחותיה עביד - בתמיה, נמצא עובר על נדרו:
Rashi on Ketubot 70b:10:1.english: And does a trustee not perform his agency - [This is] a rhetorical question: [if so,] he is found to be violating his vow.

Rashi on Ketubot 70b:11:1.hebrew: הרי אלו יכתבו ויתנו - אע"ג דלא אמר ליה לסופר "כתוב", ה"נ, אע"ג דלא אמר ליה "זון", שלוחיה הוא:
Rashi on Ketubot 70b:11:1.english: Behold, these should write and give [it] - Even though he did not say to the scribe, "Write," here too, even though he did not say to him, "Support [her]," he is his agent.

Rashi on Ketubot 70b:12:1.english: There he says, "Let him write" - [This is] an expression of command to the one who hears his voice.

Rashi on Ketubot 70b:13:1.hebrew: בדליקה התירו לומר - בשבת, דמתוך שאדם בהול על ממונו, אי לא שרית ליה אתי לכבויי:
Rashi on Ketubot 70b:13:1.english: In [the case of] a fire they permitted to say - On Shabbat, for since a person is panicked over his property, if you do not permit [this] to him, he will come to extinguish [it].

Rashi on Ketubot 70b:13:2.english: Is it not to exclude a case like this - [i.e.,] regarding all prohibitions in the Torah.

Rashi on Ketubot 70b:13:3.hebrew: שאר איסורי שבת - דחמירי, ולא התירו בהן לומר "העושה לי מלאכה זו אינו מפסיד" כדי שישמעו עובדי כוכבים ויעשו, אבל בנדרים לא גזור:
Rashi on Ketubot 70b:13:3.english: Other prohibitions of Shabbat - For they are stringent, and [the Sages] did not permit in their case to say, "Whoever performs this labor for me will not lose out," so that idolaters will hear and do [it]; however, regarding vows, they did not decree [this].

Rashi on Ketubot 70b:15:1.hebrew: דלעלמא קאמר - לא דמי לשליחות כלל, דלא ייחד איש לעשותו. אבל רגיל אצלו, אימא לא כו':
Rashi on Ketubot 70b:15:1.english: He is speaking generally - [This] does not resemble agency at all, since he did not designate a person to do it. However, [where he is] familiar with him, I might say no, etc.

Rashi on Ketubot 70b:1:1.hebrew: נעשה כאומר לה - דאע"ג דלא אמר, הרי הוא כאומר, דודאי אדעתא דהכי אדרה:
Rashi on Ketubot 70b:1:1.english: It is considered as though he is saying to her - For even though he did not say [it explicitly], it is as though he said [it], because certainly it was with this intention that he forbade her by a vow.

Rashi on Ketubot 70b:3:1.hebrew: בדלא ספקה - מזונות למעשה ידיה הקצוב לה במשנת אע"פ (לעיל כתובות דף סד:):
Rashi on Ketubot 70b:3:1.english: Where [it] is not enough - Sustenance [corresponding] to her handiwork that is allotted to her in the Mishnah [of] Af Al Pi (above, Ketubot 64b).

Rashi on Ketubot 70b:4:1.english: Behold, she is accustomed to them - And he is obligated to [provide them to] her.

Rashi on Ketubot 70b:6:1.hebrew: שהגיע זמן ולא נשאו - דמדאורייתא לא משועבד לה, לפיכך חל הנדר, דאיסור דאורייתא הוא. ומדרבנן חייב לזונה, לפיכך יעמיד פרנס:
Rashi on Ketubot 70b:6:1.english: Where the time arrived and they had not married - For by Torah law he is not obligated to [sustain] her; therefore the vow takes effect, as it is a Torah prohibition. And by rabbinic law he is obligated to sustain her; therefore he must appoint a provider.

Rashi on Ketubot 70b:8:1.hebrew: וניסת - דהשתא חייב במזונותיה, והנדר כבר חל עליו:
Rashi on Ketubot 70b:8:1.english: And she married [him] - For now he is obligated [to provide] her sustenance, and the vow has already taken effect upon him.

Rashi on Ketubot 70b:8:2.english: She considered and accepted [it] - She knew that he was forbidden to sustain her, and [yet] she married him.

Rashi on Ketubot 70b:9:1.english: With regard to blemishes - At the end of our chapter, in the Mishnah.

Rashi on Ketubot 70b:9:2.hebrew: לענין מזוני מי אמרינן - סבורה הייתי? יודעת היא שאי אפשר לה בלא מזונות:
Rashi on Ketubot 70b:9:2.english: With regard to sustenance, do we say - "I thought [I could accept it]"? She knows that it is impossible for her [to live] without sustenance.

Tosafot on Ketubot 70b:10:1.hebrew: ופרנס לאו שליחותיה קעביד - השתא סלקא דעתין דאמר ליה: "ספק לה מזונות ואני פורע". ולא דמי להא דמסקינן בריש פרק בתרא דע"ז (דף סג. ושם): "אומר אדם לחנוני הרגיל אצלו: תן פירות לחמרי ולפועלי, ואינו חושש לא משום שביעית ולא משום יין נסך" — דהתם לא קאמר ליה דליתיב להו איסורא, הלכך לאו שליחותיה עביד אי יהיב להו יין נסך; אבל הכא שליחותיה קא עביד כי יהיב לה שום מזונות:
Tosafot on Ketubot 70b:10:1.english: And does a trustee not perform his agency? - At this point [the Gemara] assumes that [the husband] said to him: "Supply her with sustenance, and I will pay [you back]." And this is not comparable to that which we conclude at the beginning of the last chapter of Avodah Zarah (63a and elsewhere): "A person may say to a shopkeeper with whom he is accustomed [to deal]: 'Give produce to my donkey-drivers and my workers,' and he need not be concerned either on account of [the laws of] the Sabbatical year or on account of libation wine" — for there he does not tell him to give them a forbidden item, therefore [the shopkeeper] is not performing his agency if he gives them libation wine; but here [the trustee] is performing his agency when he gives her any sustenance.

Tosafot on Ketubot 70b:10:2.hebrew: באומר כל הזן אינו מפסיד - ולא בעי לשנויי בחנוני הרגיל אצלו? אומר רבינו יצחק: ד"יעמיד פרנס" משמע דמפרנס לה מזונות, אבל בחנוני הרגיל אצלו לא מפרש לה. מיהו, אומר רבינו שמואל: דווקא בכי האי גוונא דאמר בסתם "כל הזן אינו מפסיד" שרי במודר הנאה, אבל למימר ליחיד "אם תזון לא תפסיד" אסור, דמיחזי כשלוחו; דגבי בא בדרך לא שרי למימר הכי. ובסוף מסקנא נמי, דמשני "לא מיבעיא כל הזן" כו', אי הוה שרי למימר ליחיד, הוה ליה למיתני בחנוני הרגיל אצלו "אם תזון לא תפסיד", והוה משמע לן רבותא טפי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 70b:10:2.english: [The Mishnah refers] to one who says: "Whoever sustains [her] will not lose out" - [Why] did [Rav Huna] not want to answer [that the Mishnah is referring] to a storekeeper who is familiar with him? Rabbeinu Yitzchak says: Because "he must appoint a trustee" implies that he provides her with sustenance, whereas [the Mishnah] does not explain it [as referring] to a storekeeper who is familiar with him. However, Rabbeinu Shmuel says: Only in such a case, where he says generally, "Whoever sustains [her] will not lose out," is it permitted for one prohibited by a vow from deriving benefit; however, to say to an individual, "If you sustain [her], you will not lose out," is forbidden, because he appears like his agent — for regarding [the case of] "one who comes on the road," it is not permitted to say thus. And at the end of the conclusion as well, where [the Gemara] answers, "It is not necessary [to say] 'whoever sustains [her],'" etc., if it were permitted to say [this] to an individual, [the Tanna] should have taught regarding a storekeeper who is familiar with him, "If you sustain [him], you will not lose out," and it would have taught us a greater novelty.

Tosafot on Ketubot 70b:1:1.hebrew: נעשה כאומר לה צאי כו' - הכא לא מצי למיפרך "והא לא אמר לה הכי", כדפריך באע"פ (לעיל כתובות דף נח:); דהכא אין אנו משנין נדר מכמו שנדר, אלא טעמא בעלמא הוא — דלמה הוא מדירה? אלא בשביל שרוצה שיהיו מעשה ידיה שלה. אבל התם, גבי מקדיש ידי אשתו, אין הנדר טוב, וצריך לתקן דיבורו שרוצה לומר "יקדשו ידיה לעושיהן"; להכי פריך לה התם:
Tosafot on Ketubot 70b:1:1.english: It is considered as though he were saying to her, "Spend [your earnings]," etc. - Here [the Gemara] cannot raise the objection, "But he did not say this to her," as it objects in [the chapter] Af Al Pi (above, Ketubot 58b); for here we are not altering [the wording of] the vow from how it was vowed, rather it is merely a reason — for why does he impose a vow upon her? Only because he wants her handiwork to be hers. However, there, regarding one who consecrates his wife's hands, the vow is not valid, and one must emend his statement [to mean] that he intends to say, "Let her hands be consecrated to their Maker"; therefore, [the Gemara] raises that objection there.

Tosafot on Ketubot 70b:2:1.hebrew: אלא לא תימא נעשה כו' - לא הוה מצי למימר דמתני' דהכא כר"מ דאמר אין אדם מוציא דבריו לבטלה, כדמשני באע"פ (שם), דלא דמי; דודאי משום דאין אדם מוציא דבריו לבטלה יש לנו לתקן דיבורו, כמו התם דמקדיש מעשה ידיה ואמרי' דבעי למימר "יקדשו ידיך לעושיהן", דאינו אלא תיקון מלה בעלמא. אבל להוסיף על הדיבור מה שלא אמר כלל — אין לנו להוסיף בשביל כך, כיון שאין לנו לומר שכך היה דעתו בלא שום דיבור אחר, כמו שהיינו סבורין מתחלה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 70b:2:1.english: Rather, do not say "it is considered," etc. - [The Gemara] could not say that the Mishnah here is in accordance with Rabbi Meir, who says [that] a person does not utter his words in vain, as it answers in [the chapter] Af Al Pi (ibid.), because [the two cases] are not comparable; for certainly, because a person does not utter his words in vain, we should emend his statement — as [in the case] there, where one consecrates his wife's earnings and we say that he meant to say, "May your hands be consecrated to their Maker" — since that is merely a correction of a word. However, to add to his statement something that he did not say at all — we should not add [it] for that reason, since we cannot say that such was his intention without any other statement, as we had initially thought.

Tosafot on Ketubot 70b:4:1.hebrew: והאידנא דאדרתן לא מצינא לאיגלגולי בהדך - ואדעתא דהכי לא מחלה שידירנה, הלכך משועבד לה; ומ"מ חל הנדר, דבשעת הנדר אכתי לא היה משועבד. אי נמי: בלא טעם מחילה הנדר חל, שכל זמן שהיא עמו יש לה לגלגל עמו — דאע"ג דאין יורדת עמו, דאין זה חשיב ירידה, דמיירי שאין בני משפחתה העשירים כמו בעלה רגילין בכך, אלא אביה מתוך עושרו היה מוותר — הלכך יש לה לגלגל עמו, וכשאינה עמו יש לה להנהיג כמו שהיתה רגילה בבית אביה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 70b:4:1.english: "And now that you have vowed, I cannot abide [the lesser lifestyle] with you" - And she did not waive [her right] with the intention that he would vow [against] her; therefore, he is obligated to her. Nevertheless, the vow takes effect, for at the time of the vow he was not yet obligated [to provide them]. Alternatively: even without the reason of waiver, the vow takes effect, for as long as she is with him she must abide [the lesser lifestyle] with him — even though [a wife] does not go down [in standard] with him, this is not considered a descent, for [the Gemara] is speaking of a case where the members of her family who are as wealthy as her husband are not accustomed to this, rather her father, out of his wealth, would indulge [her] — therefore she must abide [the lesser lifestyle] with him, and when she is not with him, she is entitled to conduct herself as she was accustomed in her father's house.

Tosafot on Ketubot 70b:6:1.hebrew: שהגיע זמן ולא נשאו - פירש בקונטרס דמדאורייתא לא משתעבד לה, לפיכך הנדר חל. וקשה: דא"כ, מן הנשואין נמי יחול הנדר מהאי טעמא, דהא קיימא לן דמזונות נשואה דרבנן! ועוד: "קונם שאני עושה לפיך" — אמאי אין הנדר חל? והא מעשה ידיה לבעלה לכ"ע לא הוי אלא מדרבנן! ונראה לפרש: "שהגיע זמן ולא נשאו" — כלו' הא דקתני "יעמיד פרנס" אשהגיע זמן ולא נשאו קאי, אבל כשנדר עדיין לא הגיע הזמן, לפיכך חל הנדר. ודוקא הגיע זמן, אבל נשאת — אין צריך להעמיד פרנס, דסברה וקיבלה, כדאמר בסמוך. ועוד י"ל: כשהדירה כבר הגיע הזמן, ומיהו חל הנדר, דלא אלמוה רבנן לשיעבודא דאשה כל זמן שלא נישאת, ומפקיע הקונם אותו שיעבוד:
Tosafot on Ketubot 70b:6:1.english: When the time had arrived and they had not [yet] married - Rashi explained that by Torah law he is not obligated to her [for sustenance], and therefore the vow takes effect. And this is difficult: for if so, even after marriage the vow should take effect for this [same] reason, since we hold as an established principle that the sustenance of a married woman is [only] rabbinic! Furthermore, [regarding a wife who vows,] "Konam [anything] that I produce for your mouth" — why does the vow not take effect? Why, her handiwork [belonging] to her husband is, according to all opinions, only rabbinic! And it appears [best] to explain "when the time had arrived and they had not [yet] married" as follows: that which [the Mishnah] teaches, "he must appoint a steward," refers to [the case] where the time had arrived and they had not [yet] married, whereas when he made the vow, the time had not yet arrived, and therefore the vow took effect. And specifically [where] the time had arrived [and they had not yet married]; however, if she married, he does not need to appoint a steward, because she considered [it] and accepted [it], as [the Gemara] states shortly below. And furthermore, one can say: when he vowed [to prohibit] her, the time had already arrived; nevertheless, the vow takes effect, because the Sages did not strengthen the obligation to a woman so long as she has not married, and thus the konam [vow] overrides that obligation.

Tosafot on Ketubot 70b:7:1.hebrew: טפי לא עביד שליחותיה - הכא לא שייך טעמא דזילותא, כיון דלא נישאת. וא"ת: ויעשה לה תקנה אחרת, כגון שיתן לו לחבירו במתנה והלה יתן לה, כמו גבי בא בדרך דמייתי לקמן, דאין לומר דווקא בא בדרך ואין לו מה יאכל התירו לו, דהא גבי מעשה דבית חורון משמע דאי הוה יהיב ליה מתנה גמורה הוה שרי אביו למיכל? וי"ל: דאין הכי נמי, אבל אין רגילות ליתן בכה"ג, דכל שעה ירא שיחזיק בהן המקבל. וא"ת: ויפקיר, כדלקמן? וי"ל: דהא ודאי לא שרינן אלא לבא בדרך, הואיל ולא נכנסו המזונות לרשות אחרת משיצאו מיד המדיר, דנראה כמו שהן עדיין ברשותו. ותקנתא דחנוני הרגיל אצלו איכא למימר נמי דלא שכיח דעבדי טפי משלשים יום, הואיל והמדיר אינו אומר לו ליתן לו מעות:
Tosafot on Ketubot 70b:7:1.english: Longer [than that, the agent] will not carry out his agency - Here the reason of degradation does not apply, since she is not [yet] married. And if you ask: Let him make another arrangement for her, such as that he should give [food] to his fellow as a gift and the latter will give [it] to her, like in the case of one traveling on the road that [the Gemara] cites below — for one cannot say that [only] specifically [for] one traveling on the road who has nothing to eat did they permit him [to do this], because regarding the incident of Beit Choron it is implied that if he had given him a complete gift, his father would have been permitted to eat [from it]? One can answer that indeed this is so, but it is not customary to give in such a manner, because at every moment he fears that the recipient will keep them [for himself]. And if you ask: Let him declare [the food] ownerless, as [mentioned] below? One can answer that this we certainly only permit for one traveling on the road, since the provisions did not enter another domain after leaving the hand of the one who made the vow, so it appears as though they are still in his domain. And [regarding] the arrangement of a storekeeper who is accustomed [to deal] with him, one can also say that it is uncommon for them to do [this] for more than thirty days, since the one who made the vow does not tell him [that he will] give him money.
